entries.violation_key: cancel_delivery(p_delivery_id uuid, p_cancel_reason text, p_performed_by uuid, p_idempotency_key text)
entries.justification: Re-reviewed live pg_get_functiondef 2026-10-20 (America/Chicago; read 2026-10-21 UTC) after replay-binding batch 3b (20261019235000, ledger 20261021024020) put a wrapper in front of the renamed body. The public wrapper binds v_actor := auth.uid() in its DECLARE, raises IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED without a key, refuses a NULL auth.uid() ('authentication required'), refuses a non-null p_performed_by that differs from v_actor ('actor mismatch', the body's own message), and requires an active admin or sales_rep profile for v_actor BEFORE check_idempotency_intent can replay anything; it fingerprints auth.uid() as actor_id, never p_performed_by. It then passes p_performed_by (NULL or equal to auth.uid()) to the postgres-only _cancel_delivery_replay_impl_20261015, which repeats the same auth.uid() / mismatch refusals, derives v_actor := COALESCE(p_performed_by, auth.uid()) (necessarily the caller), role-gates it again, and attributes every inventory, order, invoice, delivery, audit and activity write to that v_actor. The flag is predicate shape noise (the refusal compares v_actor IS DISTINCT FROM p_performed_by, with the parameter on the right, so the refusal-head pattern does not strip it), not an actor-forgery hole. The actor-forgery-fin-audit exception for this function was removed the same day: the new wrapper writes no financial_audit_log row and is no longer flagged there. Pins: the wrapper, the renamed body it delegates to, and auth.uid(); neither body calls is_admin()/is_sales_rep() (direct profiles role query), so no helper pin applies. Exception matches only the reviewed suspect parameter and exact function/dependency definition, owner, and effective EXECUTE contracts; missing or changed contracts leave the finding visible. Superseded review (2026-09-12, pre-wrapper body, md5 21da58c0c8f22d933ddd6938f5927194): same actor derivation and role gate.

entries.violation_key: start_and_complete_delivery(p_delivery_id uuid, p_signed_by text, p_delivered_on date, p_performed_by uuid, p_quantities jsonb, p_issue_type text, p_issue_notes text, p_idempotency_key text)
entries.justification: Live pg_proc read-back 2026-10-20 02:25 UTC after 20261019220000 (ledger 20261020022222, PR #964). Matched p_signed_by is text signature-name data (the receiver's printed name), not user identity, the same shape as the reviewed complete_delivery exception. The function binds v_actor := auth.uid(), raises AUTH_REQUIRED on NULL and ACTOR_MISMATCH when p_performed_by IS NOT NULL AND IS DISTINCT FROM v_actor before any work, and passes only v_actor (never p_performed_by) to confirm_delivery and complete_delivery; p_signed_by is used only in the replay fingerprint and as complete_delivery's signature-name argument. Its own admin/sales_rep or assigned-driver authorization runs before the receipt lookup, and complete_delivery's authorization still precedes writes. EXECUTE: authenticated only. This is scanner noise, not an accepted actor-forgery hole. Pins cover this function, confirm_delivery (which it calls to start), complete_delivery (which receives p_signed_by) with the two private bodies behind it that hold the authorization this relies on (_complete_delivery_replay_impl_20261015 and _complete_delivery_period_preflight_impl, as the adjacent complete_delivery exception pins them), and auth.uid(); any change to their definition, owner or EXECUTE grants un-matches this exception and the flag comes back for a fresh review.

entries.violation_key: convert_quote_to_order(p_quote_id uuid, p_performed_by uuid, p_idempotency_key text, p_expected_row_version bigint, p_below_cost_reason text)
entries.justification: Live pg_get_functiondef semantic review 2026-09-12, independently traced by RLS/migration reviewers for mutators and inspected by coordinator for the two read-only grouping reports. Public wrapper first invokes _begin_below_cost_money_write, which binds auth.uid(), rejects non-null mismatch, requires active admin/sales_rep; owner-only delegate independently repeats auth bind/refusal (13-17) before role/ownership checks (19-32). This is scanner noise, not an accepted actor-forgery hole. Exception matches only the reviewed suspect parameter and exact function/dependency definition, owner, and effective EXECUTE contracts; missing or changed contracts leave the finding visible. Reason-parser pin declined 2026-09-23 (CodeRabbit on PR #786), measured from the guard's own body: _begin_below_cost_money_write raises AUTH_REQUIRED on a NULL auth.uid(), ACTOR_MISMATCH on a non-null p_performed_by that differs from it, and INSUFFICIENT_ROLE unless the actor is an active admin/sales_rep -- ALL THREE before it ever calls public._below_cost_reason_from_json(p_payload), whose only effect is the text placed in the app.crx_below_cost_reason GUC. That call sits in the pinned guard's own definition, so the pinned digest already covers whether it is reached. The parser is IMMUTABLE SECURITY INVOKER, takes no actor argument, reads no table, and returns caller-supplied payload text the caller already controls, so no change to it can make forged attribution succeed; it is therefore not 'materially relied on in the semantic review' in the README sense. It also calls public._below_cost_reason_from_text, so pinning every transitive callee rather than every materially-relied-on dependency would expand to an unbounded closure. Pins are live database-side digests (definition+owner+ACL); none was invented here, because a wrong digest would un-match this exception permanently and turn the sweep red.

entries.violation_key: get_gross_sales_report(p_start_date date, p_end_date date, p_group_by text)
entries.justification: Live pg_get_functiondef semantic review 2026-10-20. Not actor identity: p_group_by is a text grouping selector on a STABLE, read-only report; the predicate matches it only because its name fits p_%by and the wrapper forwards it to its private implementation before any ACTOR_MISMATCH refusal (there is no actor to refuse). Neither the wrapper nor the implementation contains INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE or an exception handler, and nothing attributes a row to anyone. Migration 20261019010000 (PR #957, cost/margin admin-only, applied 2026-10-19) renamed the reviewed body unchanged to _get_gross_sales_report_cost_impl_20261019 (EXECUTE: postgres only; SECURITY INVOKER, so it runs as the wrapper's owner) and installed a SECURITY DEFINER wrapper whose first statement is PERFORM public.require_admin() (raises unless profiles.id = auth.uid() is an active admin), then RETURN QUERY from the implementation.
